decision.summaryForCoordinator: The reuse holds up. The borrowed fixture's digest reproduces at 0444 and agrees with the FX-1 catalog on id, path and sha256, so the two catalogs pinning it do not diverge, and the role claim was checked against the fixture bytes rather than the sibling catalog: the component genuinely declares all seven closed-set tokens. No new bytes were written — the pinned directory is unchanged at nineteen files with no FX-9 file, which is what a reuse-only catalog should look like. The scenario is faithful to v9: initialState records a non-interactive context with no controlling terminal and no pre-existing policy, which is the condition v9's FX-9 intent names and which makes PR-7 reachable, and live v9 defines PR-7 as consent-required-and-unavailable, adding that in a non-interactive context the family is reached without attempting a prompt and that attempting one is itself the defect FX-9 detects. The proves label is a character-for-character match to v9 and is held to ENFORCEMENT, not softened to disclosure. Nothing prohibited is authored: prompt-observation bytes, terminal traces, PR-7 refusal records and the policy document the refusal would name are each listed unauthored and each absent from the bytes, with PR-7, prompt, terminal, policy, consent and interactive all occurring zero times in the reused fixture. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 43123ccb and 0444, three of three cited digests equal live bytes, file 08 pin equal to live and unmodified, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, and neither QUALIFIED nor SATISFIED occurs anywhere. Fifteen attacks run, fifteen refuted, zero findings. Two things worth carrying: the directory now accounts exactly — nineteen on disk, nineteen authored across three catalogs, zero orphans — and eight of those nineteen fixtures are pinned by two catalogs each, so those eight can no longer be revised independently.
